Risk scenario: A former freelancer's active account is used to publish false content under the HGMN name.
Vulnerability / cause: Freelancer and contractor accounts are never reviewed.
Planned controls: Quarterly access reviews; MFA for all CMS users; joiner/mover/leaver process for contractors; approval step for sensitive publishing.

Risk scenario: Ransomware on the broadcast network takes playout off-air for more than 4 hours.
Vulnerability / cause: Broadcast systems patched ad hoc; playout restore never tested; broadcast network not monitored.
Existing controls: Offsite backups; physical access control at HQ master control.
Planned controls: Segment the broadcast network; documented patch process; offline backups; test playout restore twice a year; extend monitoring to broadcast.

Risk scenario: A confidential journalist source identity is exposed through a compromised tool or an insider.
Vulnerability / cause: Source-protection data is not classified; access is not limited to need-to-know.
Existing controls: Encryption of subscriber data at rest (does not cover source data).
Planned controls: Define and apply a source-data classification; restrict access; encrypt; add data leakage monitoring; staff briefing.
Risk owner (role): CISO with Head of Editorial Standards

Risk scenario: A DDoS attack disrupts live streaming during a major event.
Vulnerability / cause: Lessons from a past DDoS were noted but not tracked to closure; capacity not tested.
Planned controls: DDoS response playbook; capacity test before major events; track lessons learned to closure.

Risk scenario: An official social media account is taken over through phishing and used to post false statements.
Vulnerability / cause: Awareness training at onboarding only; no phishing simulations; no account inventory.
Planned controls: Hardware-key MFA; account inventory and owners; regular phishing simulations; takeover response steps.
Risk owner (role): Head of Social Media and Communications

Risk scenario: A journalist's phone or laptop is compromised by targeted spear-phishing or spyware.
Vulnerability / cause: Field equipment and freelancer laptops are not inventoried; training is onboarding only.
Existing controls: Central log collection (does not cover field devices).
Planned controls: Inventory field kit; managed devices; mobile threat defence; travel security briefings; incident reporting channel.

Risk scenario: A breach of subscriber personal data occurs and notification to individuals and the regulator is delayed.
Vulnerability / cause: No pre-approved external communications or breach notification procedure.
Existing controls: Encryption of subscriber data at rest.
Planned controls: Breach notification SOP aligned to PDPPL Article 14; legal register; pre-approved communications templates.

Risk scenario: A supplier outage or compromise disrupts the website and streaming platform.
Vulnerability / cause: No supplier security assessment process; contracts not reviewed for security terms.
Planned controls: Contract security and SLA clauses; supplier security questionnaire; exit and failover plan; review cyber insurance cover.

Risk scenario: Unauthorised physical access to a regional bureau leads to theft of equipment or footage.
Vulnerability / cause: Physical security at bureaus is weaker than at HQ.
Planned controls: Accept at Medium pending a baseline; low-cost measures only (visitor log, device encryption). Formal acceptance by the COO, signature and date required. Review in 6 months.

Asset: All critical systems S1 to S8
Risk scenario: An intrusion goes undetected for days because there is no 24/7 monitoring and the incident response plan has never been tested.
Vulnerability / cause: Business-hours monitoring only; outsourced alerts with no triage criteria; IR plan untested.
Existing controls: Central log collection; outsourced alert service.
Planned controls: Define alert triage criteria; run a tabletop exercise; extend monitoring to broadcast; decide on 24/7 coverage.
